title: What Separates Remote Work Winners from Remote Work Losers
author: Trubman, Russ
summary: Trubman analyzes what differentiates successful remote teams from struggling ones after years of remote work experience. The winner is not determined by technology, policies, or communication tools. Successful remote cultures are built on clarity about what matters, strong relationships that exist and are maintained intentionally, and deliberate practices to maintain connection and accountability. Remote work losers fail because they try to replicate office dynamics instead of building the culture remote work actually requires and enables.
points: Remote work success is not about tools or policies but about culture and clarity.
Strong relationships must exist and be maintained intentionally in remote environments.
Winners build culture appropriate to remote work instead of trying to replicate offices.
Clarity about expectations and what matters is more critical in remote work.
Remote work success requires different management practices, not just a change of location.
The best remote teams are intentional about culture in ways office teams often are not.
